title: One Point Lesson - Gland Packing Replacement (PTFE 4526L) (OPL-YD-2301-02)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-YD-2301-02 - Gland Packing Replacement (PTFE 4526L).

Equipment: YD-2301 (POLYMER FLUID BED DRYER), Discipline: Mechanical, Area: 2300 – POWDER DRYING SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-5500 (SIL 2), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-2301.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
Gland packing replacement (ptfe 4526l) for YD-2301 (POLYMER FLUID BED DRYER) in the POWDER DRYING SYSTEM. Worn gland packing lets powder and steam leak at the drum ends. This is the most frequent YD-2301 maintenance job and a housekeeping/safety issue.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Apply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
- Precaution 2: Isolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.
- Precaution 3: Wear the correct PPE: coverall, safety shoes, gloves, goggles and hearing protection.
- Precaution 4: Beware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
- Precaution 5: Use certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Standard mechanical hand tools & calibrated torque wrench
- Tool 2: LOTO padlocks and permit
- Tool 3: Laser/dial alignment kit (as applicable)
- Tool 4: Feeler gauges, dial indicator, seal/bearing pullers
- Tool 5: Correct spare parts and gaskets per the BOM
- Tool 6: Lifting gear and slings (certified)

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Isolate steam and N2, drain condensate, and LOTO the drive
- Step 1 - Check: Isolation & LOTO verified
- Step 2 - Action: Remove the old PTFE rings (8 pcs 4526L at discharge, 2 pcs 4505L at feed)
- Step 2 - Check: Parts match BOM / spec
- Step 3 - Action: Fit new rings one at a time, staggering the joints by 90 deg
- Step 3 - Check: Torque / clearance to spec
- Step 4 - Action: Tighten the gland follower evenly - snug only, never over-torque
- Step 4 - Check: No leak / smooth operation
- Step 5 - Action: Warm through slowly and re-check for leaks, re-nip after 24 h
- Step 5 - Check: Record in equipment history

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Steam and powder leaking at YD-2301 discharge gland | Likely Cause: PTFE 4526L gland packing worn beyond service limit | Action: Replaced 8 pcs PTFE 4526L packing, staggered joints, re-nipped after
- Symptom: Minor powder weep at feed-end gland | Likely Cause: PTFE 4505L packing hardened and worn | Action: Renewed 2 pcs PTFE 4505L feed-end packing
- Symptom: SSLL-2305 speed low alarm, chain slack observed | Likely Cause: Chain elongation with normal wear caused slip | Action: Adjusted take-up, lubricated chain, checked sprocket wear

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: Worn gland packing lets powder and steam leak at the drum ends. This is the most frequent YD-2301 maintenance job and a housekeeping/safety issue.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-5500: e.g. TSHH-2301 trips at > 125 degC - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-2301 before working on YD-2301.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
